newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan activists blocked from reaching islands.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan activists blocked from reaching islands.

text.p: Chinese nationalists from Taiwan were thwarted in another bid to reach a disputed East China Sea archipelago on Tuesday, sailing away after a skirmish with Japanese patrols defending Tokyo's claim of sovereignty.

The secretive overnight voyage to the islands, known in Chinese as the Diaoyus and in Japanese as the Senkakus, was timed to coincide with Hong Kong's handover to China, the activists told state media.
Organiser Ching Chieh-shou said three Japanese ships blocked his boat three to four nautical miles from the uninhabited islands, held by Japan but claimed by both Taiwan and China.
Ching said the captain of his fishing boat decided to turn back, citing safety concerns.
Japan's Maritime Safety Agency said the Taiwan vessel, with about 14 people aboard, was stopped early on Tuesday by coast guard vessels four miles off the main island in the chain.
Four activists tried to jump aboard a Japanese patrol boat while others threw plastic bottles. The Taiwan boat motored off after the hour-long skirmish, an agency spokesman said. No one was injured.
"It appears they tried to land on the island to coincide with the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule," the spokesman said.
The group had planned to approach the archipelago at midnight Monday -- the moment Britain handed Hong Kong over to China, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
Ching told local media that he decided to sail secretly to avoid the kind of mass publicity that he said helped Tokyo thwart a much larger landing mission in May.

The island chain has ignited fiery nationalist passions in Chinese communities in Hong Kong and Taiwan since a Japanese right-wing group built a makeshift lighthouse there in July 1996, a move they said bolstered Japan's sovereignty.
China says the islets have been Chinese territory for centuries while Japan's claim dates to 1894.
The islands' waters are rich in fish, but experts have said there is no evidence they hold significant oil deposits.
